title: Traffic Light
description: Build a mini traffic light with a red, a yellow and a green LED, then program the Arduino to cycle green, yellow, red just like a real crossing.

steps.clip: Let's build a traffic light! Grab your Arduino Uno, a breadboard, a red, a yellow and a green LED, three 220 ohm resistors, some jumper wires and the USB cable.
Start with the red light. Push a 220 ohm resistor into the top half of the breadboard so its two legs sit in two different columns.
hints: Leave a couple of columns between the resistor's legs, for example columns 3 and 6.
A resistor works either way round.

steps.clip: Run a jumper wire from pin 12 on the Arduino to the column holding the resistor's left leg.
hints: Any free hole in the same column-half as the resistor leg works.
Pin 12 is on the digital header, next to pin 13.

steps.clip: Take the red LED. Push its long leg into the column with the resistor's right leg, and its short leg into the next column over.
hints: The long leg is the anode: it goes toward the resistor.
Don't put both LED legs in the same column.

steps.clip: Connect the red LED's short leg to ground: run a black wire from its column to a GND pin on the Arduino.
hints: There's a GND pin right next to pin 13.
Use a fresh hole in the short leg's column.

steps.clip: Now the yellow light. Push a second 220 ohm resistor into the top half, a few columns to the right of the red LED.
hints: Keep it well clear of the red LED's columns, for example columns 11 and 14.
Each leg in its own column.

steps.clip: Run a wire from pin 11 to the column holding this resistor's left leg.
hints: Pin 11 is right next to pin 12.
Use any free hole in that column.

steps.clip: Take the yellow LED. Long leg into the resistor's right-leg column, short leg into the next column.
hints: Long leg toward the resistor.
Short leg in its own column.

steps.clip: Run a black wire from the yellow LED's short leg column to another GND pin.
hints: The power header has two more GND pins.
All GND pins are the same connection.

steps.clip: Last, the green light. Push the third 220 ohm resistor into the top half, further to the right again.
hints: For example columns 19 and 22.
Each leg in its own column.

steps.clip: Run a wire from pin 10 to the column holding this resistor's left leg.
hints: Pin 10 is right next to pin 11.
Any free hole in that column works.

steps.clip: Take the green LED. Long leg into the resistor's right-leg column, short leg into the next column.
hints: Long leg toward the resistor.
Reversed, the LED won't light.

steps.clip: Finish by running a black wire from the green LED's short leg column to the last GND pin.
hints: Any GND pin works.
Use a fresh hole in the short leg's column.

steps.clip: Plug in the USB cable and upload the code. Watch your light go green, then yellow, then red, over and over!
